start.title: Morning
start.text:
Morning light has begun to find its way through the curtains.

You wake slowly beneath sheets that had been considerably neater when you went to sleep.

For a few moments there is nothing demanding your attention.

No summons. No tutor. No attendant hovering at the bedside with some carefully worded reminder of where you ought already to be.

Only the quiet of your chambers and the vague awareness that the rest of the palace has been awake for some time.

choices.flavourText:
You throw the covers aside before comfort has the opportunity to make a convincing argument.

There is a day waiting for you.

choices.text: Stay where you are a little longer.
choices.flavourText:
You close your eyes again.

Not to sleep.

Simply because there are few luxuries quite so satisfying as knowing you ought to get up and choosing not to.

You reach for the bell beside the bed.

There is little reason to begin the morning by making everything more difficult than it needs to be.

the_room.title: The Room
the_room.text:
By the time you are properly awake, sunlight has crept farther across the floor.

Your chambers look much as they always do.

Books lie where you left them. A half-finished cup from the previous evening has somehow escaped collection. Fresh flowers have appeared on the table near the balcony doors without your noticing anyone bring them.

Someone has already opened the inner shutters.

Beyond the closed balcony doors comes the distant murmur of the palace beginning its day.

You stretch.

Whatever you decide to do with the morning, you should probably look presentable first.

the_mirror.title: The Mirror
the_mirror.text:
The mirror is less forgiving than the morning light.

Your hair has made several decisions during the night without consulting you.

Brushes, pins, powders and pigments occupy their usual places nearby.

choices.flavourText:
There is nothing wrong with wanting to look good.

Hair first. Then the smaller details.

Nothing excessive, but enough that the finished result looks deliberate rather than merely acceptable.

choices.text: Make yourself respectable and leave it there.
choices.flavourText:
A little effort is expected.

There is no need to dedicate half the morning to it.

You correct the worst of your hair and decide the rest can remain as it is.

Anyone distressed by the result is free to look elsewhere.

a_knock_at_the_door.title: A Knock at the Door
a_knock_at_the_door.text:
You have barely finished when someone knocks.

An attendant enters after receiving permission, carrying a tray of fruit, bread and a small pot of something hot.

She takes one look at the state of the room.

Then at you.

Then back at the room.

There is the faintest suggestion of judgement in the pause.

"You are awake."

It is delivered with such perfect neutrality that it somehow sounds accusatory.

choices.flavourText:
Her expression remains perfectly composed.

Almost.
She bows her head and begins setting out breakfast.

choices.text: Say nothing and let her work.
choices.flavourText: There is no particular need to turn every morning interaction into conversation.

breakfast.title: Breakfast
breakfast.text:
Breakfast is light.

You eat near the open window while the attendant quietly restores some degree of order to the room behind you.

The palace is louder now.

Footsteps pass beyond your door. Somewhere farther down the corridor someone is speaking far too energetically for this hour.

You catch fragments as servants move past.

Your father is already occupied.

The council assembled early.

Someone has requested additional space in the training court.

And apparently your magical tutor has already asked whether you intend to appear today.

None of this constitutes a summons.

Not yet.

You finish the last of the fruit.

dressing.title: Dressing
dressing.text:
Clothing has already been laid out for you.

The selection is elegant, carefully matched and entirely appropriate for the King's daughter.

Which is precisely why someone else chose it.

There are alternatives in the wardrobe.

choices.flavourText:
It was chosen well.

There is little virtue in rejecting something simply because another person had the good sense to select it first.

You keep the better pieces and discard the rest.

Something presentable without being unnecessarily elaborate.

choices.text: Choose something easier to move in.
choices.flavourText:
You ignore the prepared clothes altogether.

The alternative is simpler, closer fitting and considerably less likely to become irritating if the day turns active.

It will do.

the_corridor.title: The Corridor
the_corridor.text:
Outside your chambers, the palace is fully awake.

Servants move between rooms carrying linens, documents and breakfast trays. Two officials stop speaking as you approach, bow, then resume their conversation once you have passed.

A pair of younger relatives hurry across an adjoining corridor before someone calls after them.

You know these halls well enough to walk them without thinking.

Past the inner court.

Along the colonnade.

Then toward the doors overlooking the eastern gardens.

Nothing unusual has happened.

There is something pleasant about that.

the_balcony.title: The Balcony
the_balcony.text:
You push open the doors.

The world expands.

Morning lies across the city beyond the royal compound.

Pale buildings descend through terraces, courtyards and formal gardens. Water catches the light between columns. Ancient compounds sit behind high walls softened by trees cultivated over generations.

Beyond them all rises the forest.

Not a scattering of woodland around a city.

The forest.

It surrounds everything, swallowing the horizon in green.

You have stood here countless times.

Usually you scarcely think about the view.

It is simply home.

For a while you rest your hands against the stone railing and watch the city below.

Eventually, the question of what to do with yourself returns.

Your father is sitting with his councillors.

The training courts will be active by now.

Your magical instruction remains available, whether or not your tutor's patience does.

For once, the morning is largely yours.

choices.text: Decide how to spend the morning.

choose_the_day.title: How Will You Spend the Morning?

choices.flavourText:
You have spent enough time hearing what will someday be expected of you.

It might be useful to watch how those expectations are actually fulfilled.

There are few problems improved by neglecting practice.

And considerably fewer instructors willing to accept that as an excuse.

Progress has an irritating habit of requiring effort.

Your tutor would certainly agree.
